QF.id: Securities Types Features and Asset Allocation Concepts_4

question.text: In the event of liquidation of a company, equity shareholders have a 'residual claim' on assets. This means they are paid:

answer.text: Last, after all other claimants including government, lenders, employees, and preference shareholders
First, before any other claims are settled
Only if the company's total debt is less than Rs.10 crore

explanation.text: The Logic: Equity shareholders are ranked last for both profit sharing and claims on the company's assets. On liquidation, proceeds are paid first to other claimants such as the government, lenders, and employees, then to preference shareholders, and any residual amount goes to equity shareholders. The Trap: Option B reverses the priority order. Option C ignores the priority structure entirely. Option D introduces an arbitrary monetary threshold that is not part of the priority of claims. Note: "Residual claim" by definition means equity shareholders receive only what remains after all higher-ranked claims have been met.
